chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali Al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the wet mouse that had fallen into the water and was walking upon the clothes: 'Is one to pray in them?' He said: 'Wash what you see of its trace, and what you do not see, so sprinkle it with water.'
ai.seo_question: How to purify clothes touched by a wet mouse according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) establishes the principle of 'istishab al-taharah' (presumption of purity) by distinguishing between visible impurity (najasah) requiring washing and invisible traces requiring mere sprinkling (tanfih). It reflects the Shia juristic methodology of applying practical certainty to ritual cleanliness, ensuring that believers are not burdened by excessive doubt in daily worship.
